newsitem.title: UK: BritGas objects to new Ofgas restructuring plans.
newsitem.headline: BritGas objects to new Ofgas restructuring plans.

text.p: TransCo, the pipeline arm of British Gas, has objected to radical plans put forward by gas industry regulator Ofgas for further dismantling of the company, a TransCo spokswoman said on Thursday.
"TransCo sent a letter (to Ofgas) yesterday objecting to an article in The Times quoting Clare Spottiswoode directly on Ofgas's solutions to regulation," the spokeswoman said.
Spottiswoode, the Director General of Ofgas, suggested in The Times article on Wednesday that more of its operations, including its computer networks and siteworks, could be hived off to contractors.
A spokesman for Ofgas said the article was "substantially correct."
But TransCo said that the proposals had not been discussed with the company.
"The article suggests that Ofgas is considering radical plans...which are under discussion with British Gas. This is patently incorrect," the spokeswoman said.
Certain restructuring plans such as the unbundling of storage and metering were already under discussion, she said.
"We are prepared for a certain amount of unbundling, but not the unbundling of the company," said the TransCo spokeswoman.
Ofgas confirmed that it had received a letter from TransCo.
"Nothing we have been saying hasn't been said before," the Ofgas spokesman said. "It has always been our intention to reduce regulation of TransCo as much as possible by unbundling."
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission is currently examining Ofgas demands for tough Transco price controls. It is due to report in April.
British Gas is in the final stages of spinning off its gas supply business into a new company, Centrica. Shareholders are due to vote on the demerger plans on February 12.
